title: heater
description: v0.1 device-model entity: a fuel-fired space heater that reports its own operating phase and faults, one per heater, published under renewvan/heater/<id>/<property>, all retained. Named for what the hardware is, not the brand (ADR 0008); first source is an Autoterm AIR 2D read over UART by renewvan/driver-autoterm. Unknown is absent: a value the heater cannot supply is an empty retained payload (ADR 0008 'no value'), never null and never 0, so a missing sensor is not mistaken for a reading. `phase` is our name for what the status code means and is optional: it is absent (empty retained payload) only while the status code is unmapped, and `status_code` is always published beside it so an unknown code still shows something. There is no fault phase: `error_code` is independent of `phase` and can be non-zero in any phase. `ventilating` is true only for status 3.35 (fan only, unverified on hardware), otherwise absent. `commands_enabled` is published by the Driver and defaults to false: when false every command below is ignored, except `commands_enabled/set` (true or false, not persisted: a Driver restart returns to its config file). Command topics (unretained, strict JSON, not separate schema files, per ADR 0013): `renewvan/heater/<id>/set` carries true (start) or false (stop), never a toggle; `mode/set` carries a JSON string; `setpoint_c/set` an integer 1-30; `power_level/set` an integer 0-9; `thermostat/set` true or false; `ventilating/set` true or false; `clear_error/set` true only; the Driver refuses `clear_error/set` with a WARNING until it is verified on hardware, and accepts `ventilating/set` from driver-autoterm v0.4.0 although its 0x23 frame is not yet bench-verified. Per phase: `set` true starts only from phase off with error_code 0, using the settings the heater reported; `ventilating/set` true starts fan-only (using the read power_level) only from phase off and is confirmed only by status 3.35; settings writes are refused during shutting_down and while ventilating (accepted in standby), and start and every settings write re-read the heater's settings first and change only the commanded field (bytes the Driver does not understand, such as the work time, are sent back as read; a write is confirmed by the commanded field alone, since the heater rewrites power_level while running in a temperature mode); stop is always accepted. `clear_error/set` rests on an unverified frame and never starts the heater. A rejected command produces no reply topic (the Driver logs a WARNING): a command is confirmed only when the retained field changes, so a consumer shows 'pending' and times out. A consumer treats the heater as unknown whenever the owning Driver's health is not `online` or is absent; after stale_after_s (5 s) without telemetry the Driver rejects commands and clears the live fields (empty retained payloads); an instance whose live fields are absent is unknown, not invalid. The Driver never stops or re-commands the heater by itself. Verified on an AIR 2D (2026-11-02): status codes 0.1, 1.0, 1.1, 2.0, 2.1, 2.2, 2.6, 2.3, 2.4, 3.0 and 4.0 over one start-run-stop cycle. Verified on the same heater (2026-11-13): mode, setpoint_c and power_level writes, a setpoint change while running, and Thermostat (wait_mode 1) with its 3.4/3.5 standby. UNVERIFIED (confidence Low-Medium): status code 3.35 (so its `ventilating` handling), the 0x0D unblock, the clear_error frame, the setpoint_c bounds, stop from standby, and early stop; a human-present bench check is needed first. Logger view: static driver, name, commands_enabled; slow-changing mode, setpoint_c, power_level, thermostat, phase, status_code, error_code; continuous the temperatures, voltage_v, fan_rpm, fuel_pump_hz, runtime_s. See docs/adr/0021-writable-heater-and-its-command-safety-rules.md.

driver.description: Optional, retained. The key of the Driver publishing this instance: the <driver> segment of renewvan/<driver>/info, published as renewvan/heater/<id>/driver. Same slug rule as driver-info.schema.json. Identity field. A consumer must tolerate it being absent and then attributes the instance to every Driver whose info `publishes` lists 'heater'.

name.description: Optional, retained. The human label and the only label on the wire.

phase.description: Optional. Our name for what the status code means, mapped by the Driver; absent only while the status code is unmapped (an unknown code), never a fault state. Mapping verified on hardware for 0.1, 1.0-2.6, 3.0 and 4.0 (2026-11-02) and 3.4 and 3.5 (standby, 2026-11-13); 3.35 (running) is an unverified default. `standby` is the Thermostat pause: burner off (3.4 purging, 3.5 waiting), and the heater re-ignites by itself when the temperature drops.

status_code.description: The heater's raw status as 'major.minor', e.g. "3.0". A string, never a number. Always published, including for a code the Driver does not map (then `phase` is absent).

error_code.description: 0 means no fault. The contract promises only zero versus non-zero. Independent of `phase`: there is no fault phase, and a non-zero error can accompany any phase.

internal_temperature_c.description: Temperature at the heater's internal sensor, degrees Celsius.

heater_temperature_c.description: Optional. Heat exchanger temperature, degrees Celsius.

external_temperature_c.description: Optional. External probe temperature, degrees Celsius; absent when no probe is fitted (the 0x7F sentinel).

setpoint_c.description: Optional. Target temperature as read back from the heater, degrees Celsius. Bounds are unverified.

power_level.description: Optional. Power level as read back from the heater.

mode.description: Optional. Control mode as read back from the heater. controller_temperature is excluded in v1.

runtime_s.description: Optional. Seconds since the current run started.

fan_rpm.description: Optional. Fan speed in rpm (the heater's byte x 60).

fuel_pump_hz.description: Optional. Fuel pump frequency in Hz, to 2 decimals.

thermostat.description: Optional. Whether Thermostat is on, read back from the heater's wait_mode byte (1 true, 2 false; absent for any other value, e.g. a heater where it was never set). With it on, a temperature mode stops the burner above the setpoint (phase standby) instead of only turning it down. Bench-verified on an AIR 2D, 2026-11-13.

ventilating.description: Optional. True only while the heater is in fan-only mode (status 3.35); absent otherwise. When present, status_code must be "3.35" and phase "running".

commands_enabled.description: Whether the Driver accepts commands. Defaults to false; renewvan/heater/<id>/commands_enabled/set changes it until the Driver restarts; see ADR 0021.
